collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — GOOD, BAD AND ORDINARY DAYS (DAY-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Wonderful days, rotten days, mixed days and days when nothing much happens at all. Moods come without reasons, small things matter more than they should, and nobody has to end the day happier, wiser or more productive than they started it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager has found the perfect skipping stone at the calm lagoon: throw it, or keep it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has found the perfect skipping stone: flat, smooth, round, just the right weight. (subject.He/she) has been looking for one like it for years. (subject.He/she) is standing at the edge of the calm lagoon with it in (subject.his/her) hand. (friend) has stopped to watch. This is going to be the one.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) throws. The stone skips. Three. Five. Eight. Eleven. It keeps going, smaller and smaller, until it's just a ripple near the far side. They both stand there with their mouths open. "Eleven!" says (friend). "TWELVE," says (subject). They argue about it happily all the way home.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) can't bring (subject.him/her)self to throw it. It's too perfect. If (subject.he/she) throws it, it's gone. (subject.He/she) puts it in (subject.his/her) pocket and throws an ordinary stone instead, which skips twice and sinks. (friend) laughs. (subject) keeps the perfect stone for years. Sometimes (subject.he/she) takes it out and thinks about how far it would have gone.
